concepts.name: Function as input-output rule
concepts.summary: Explain that a function assigns exactly one output to each input and describe it as a rule, table, or mapping.

concepts.name: Function notation f(x)
concepts.summary: Read and interpret f(x) as the output for input x and evaluate f(3) by substitution.

concepts.name: Coordinate plane and ordered pairs
concepts.summary: Recall how to name and locate points (x, y) using the axes and quadrants.

concepts.name: Table of values plotting
concepts.summary: Build a table of input-output values and plot the points to show the shape of a graph.

concepts.name: Domain and range meaning
concepts.summary: Describe domain as the set of allowed inputs and range as the set of resulting outputs.

concepts.name: Vertical line test
concepts.summary: Use the vertical line test to decide whether a graph represents a function.

misconceptions.text: f(x) means f multiplied by x.
A function can give two different outputs for the same input, as long as the rule is consistent.
In an ordered pair (x, y), the y-value is plotted first along the horizontal axis.

concepts.name: Linear function graphs
concepts.summary: Sketch a linear function from its gradient and y-intercept and read these from its equation.

concepts.name: Intercepts of a graph
concepts.summary: Find x-intercepts by setting f(x)=0 and the y-intercept by evaluating f(0).

concepts.name: Finding domain and range
concepts.summary: Determine domain and range from an equation or graph, including restrictions such as division by zero and square roots of negatives.

concepts.name: Quadratic graph features
concepts.summary: Sketch a parabola identifying its vertex, axis of symmetry, intercepts and direction of opening.

concepts.name: Translations of graphs
concepts.summary: Apply y = f(x) + k and y = f(x - h) to shift a graph and describe the resulting movement.

concepts.name: Interval notation
concepts.summary: Write domains and ranges using inequalities and interval notation with correct open and closed ends.

concepts.name: Evaluating and interpreting graphs
concepts.summary: Read function values, solve f(x)=k and identify where a function is increasing or decreasing from its graph.

misconceptions.text: y = f(x - 2) moves the graph 2 units to the left.
The range of a function is always all real numbers.
A graph only has an x-intercept if it also has a y-intercept.

concepts.name: Stretches and reflections
concepts.summary: Apply y = af(x), y = f(bx), y = -f(x) and y = f(-x) and describe their effect on key points.

concepts.name: Combining graph transformations
concepts.summary: Determine the correct order of multiple transformations and deduce the equation of a transformed graph.

concepts.name: Composite functions
concepts.summary: Form and evaluate f(g(x)), recognise that fg differs from gf, and find the domain of the composite.

concepts.name: One-to-one and restricted domains
concepts.summary: Use the horizontal line test to decide if an inverse exists and restrict the domain to create one.

concepts.name: Inverse functions
concepts.summary: Find f⁻¹ algebraically, link its graph to a reflection in y = x and explain the swap of domain and range.

concepts.name: Piecewise-defined functions
concepts.summary: Evaluate and sketch piecewise functions, including absolute value, handling endpoints and continuity.

concepts.name: Exponential function graphs
concepts.summary: Sketch y = a^x for a>1 and 0<a<1, showing the y-intercept, horizontal asymptote and growth or decay.

misconceptions.text: f(g(x)) is always the same as g(f(x)).
y = f(2x) stretches the graph horizontally by a factor of 2.

concepts.name: Logarithmic functions as inverses
concepts.summary: Analyse y = log_a x as the inverse of y = a^x and derive its domain, range, vertical asymptote and intercept.

concepts.name: Rational function structure
concepts.summary: Analyse how factors of numerator and denominator determine zeros, vertical asymptotes and holes.

concepts.name: Asymptote determination
concepts.summary: Find vertical, horizontal and oblique asymptotes using denominator zeros and degree comparison, and explain end behaviour.

concepts.name: Even and odd symmetry
concepts.summary: Test f(-x) to classify functions as even, odd or neither and link this to reflective or rotational symmetry.

concepts.name: Sketching from key features
concepts.summary: Combine intercepts, asymptotes, sign analysis and symmetry to produce and justify a sketch of a rational graph.

concepts.name: Transformations of log and exponential
concepts.summary: Determine how transformations move asymptotes, intercepts and domain or range of exponential and log graphs.

concepts.name: Modelling with function graphs
concepts.summary: Evaluate which function family fits a context, and interpret parameters and limitations of the fitted graph.

misconceptions.text: A common factor cancelled from a rational function leaves no trace on the graph.
A graph can never cross its horizontal asymptote.
Every function that is not even must be odd.

concepts.name: Function behaviour near singularities
concepts.summary: Evaluate behaviour on each side of a discontinuity or asymptote and justify classification as hole, jump or infinite.

concepts.name: Domain-aware inverse and composition
concepts.summary: Evaluate when compositions and inverses are valid, including the identity (f∘g)⁻¹ = g⁻¹∘f⁻¹ and domain consequences.

concepts.name: Designing functions to specification
concepts.summary: Create a function with prescribed intercepts, asymptotes, symmetry and domain, and verify it meets them.

concepts.name: Comparing growth rates
aliases: polynomial vs exponential vs log growth
concepts.summary: Judge relative long-run growth of logarithmic, polynomial and exponential functions and justify with graphs.

concepts.name: Linearising data by transformation
concepts.summary: Design log or semi-log transformations that turn power and exponential relationships into straight lines to estimate parameters.

concepts.name: Parametric families of graphs
concepts.summary: Evaluate how changing a parameter alters the qualitative features and number of intercepts or asymptotes in a family of functions.

concepts.name: Critiquing graphical arguments
concepts.summary: Assess when a graph, window or technology output misleads about domain, asymptotes or solutions and correct it.

misconceptions.text: A polynomial such as x^100 will eventually overtake any exponential function such as 1.01^x.
If a graphing tool shows a smooth line through a point, the function is defined and continuous there.
The inverse of a composite fg is f⁻¹g⁻¹ in the same order.
